objectives: Survey pathogen classes + host immune responses + immune-evasion mechanisms.
Compare vaccine platforms: live-attenuated, inactivated, subunit, conjugate, mRNA, viral vector.
Trace landmark vaccination programs from smallpox eradication to COVID-19.

slides.title: Pathogen classes + host responses + immune evasion
slides.body:
**Four major pathogen classes** elicit different protective immune responses, organized around the cellular location + biology of the pathogen.

**Viruses** — obligate intracellular; cytosolic or vesicular replication.
- **Innate sensing**: TLR3 (dsRNA), TLR7/8 (ssRNA), TLR9 (CpG DNA), RIG-I/MDA5, cGAS-STING.
- **Effectors**: Type I IFN antiviral state, NK cells, **CD8 cytotoxic T cells** (the central anti-viral effector), neutralizing antibodies (block entry).
- **Memory**: long-lived plasma cells (decades, e.g., measles) + memory B + memory CD8 T cells.
- **Evasion**: antigenic variation (**influenza** drift + shift, **HIV** SHM-driven escape), latency (herpesviruses), MHC-I downregulation (CMV, KSHV), interferon antagonism (most viruses encode IFN antagonists — influenza NS1, SARS-CoV-2 ORF6, hepatitis C NS3/4A).

**Bacteria** — extracellular or intracellular; structurally diverse.
- **Extracellular** (e.g., *S. pneumoniae*, *S. aureus*, *N. meningitidis*): handled primarily by antibodies + complement + neutrophils. Pneumococcal capsule is a major virulence factor + vaccine target.
- **Intracellular** (e.g., **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**, *Listeria*, *Salmonella*): require Th1 + macrophage activation + CD8 T cells. **Mtb** persists in phagolysosomes by inhibiting maturation + uses dormancy + granuloma residence; one-third of the world is latently infected.
- **Innate sensing**: TLR2 (lipopeptides), TLR4 (LPS), TLR5 (flagellin), TLR9 (CpG), NOD1/2 (peptidoglycan), inflammasome (flagellin → NLRC4, others).
- **Evasion**: capsules (anti-phagocytic), antigenic variation (gonococcus pilin, *Borrelia* VlsE), intracellular niches, toxin secretion.

**Fungi** — yeasts (e.g., *Candida*, *Cryptococcus*) + filamentous (*Aspergillus*, *Pneumocystis*).
- **Innate sensing**: **Dectin-1** (β-glucan), **Dectin-2** + Mincle (mannans), **TLR2**.
- **Adaptive**: **Th17** (IL-17 + IL-22; recruit neutrophils + induce AMPs) — critical for mucosal fungal control. **CARD9** deficiency → chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.
- **Opportunistic** in HIV (Pneumocystis, Cryptococcus), neutropenia (Aspergillus), CMC.

**Parasites** — protozoa (*Plasmodium*, *Leishmania*, *Trypanosoma*) + helminths (worms).
- **Protozoa**: vary; *Plasmodium* hepatic + RBC stages — antibodies + CD4/CD8 T cells. Antigenic variation (*Plasmodium* PfEMP1, *Trypanosoma* VSG).
- **Helminths**: large, multicellular, extracellular tissue parasites. Drive **Th2** response: IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, eosinophils, mast cells, IgE, goblet-cell mucus + smooth-muscle contraction ("weep + sweep"). Th2 evolved largely for parasites; in industrialized settings the same axis underlies allergy + asthma (hygiene hypothesis, Strachan; old-friends hypothesis, Rook).

**Major immune-evasion strategies**:
- **Antigenic variation**: HIV (SHM-driven envelope evolution within host); influenza (antigenic drift via HA/NA point mutation; antigenic shift via reassortment of segmented genome — pandemic risk).
- **Latency**: HSV in neurons, EBV + CMV in lymphocytes, VZV in DRG, HBV cccDNA, HIV proviral reservoirs.
- **Mycobacterium tuberculosis dormancy**: persists in granulomas for decades; partially-permissive immune state.
- **MHC interference**: HSV ICP47 blocks TAP; CMV down-regulates MHC-I via multiple genes; HIV Nef down-regulates MHC-I + CD4.
- **Interferon antagonism**: nearly universal among viruses.
- **Decoy + immune-suppressive proteins**: hepatitis B sAg decoy; pox virus encodes its own cytokine decoy receptors; herpes encodes IL-10 mimics.

Understanding pathogen biology + host response shapes vaccine + therapeutic design.

slides.title: Vaccine platforms: live-attenuated, inactivated, subunit, conjugate, mRNA, viral vector
slides.body:
**Live-attenuated** — weakened but replication-competent pathogen.
- Examples: smallpox (vaccinia), measles, mumps, rubella (MMR), varicella, yellow fever (17D), oral polio (Sabin OPV), rotavirus, BCG (TB), influenza (FluMist), oral typhoid Ty21a.
- Pros: single dose often sufficient; durable + broad immunity (mimics natural infection); strong CD8 + CD4 + antibody.
- Cons: cold-chain requirements; theoretical reversion (OPV vaccine-associated paralytic polio — VAPP); contraindicated in immunocompromised + pregnancy.

**Inactivated (whole-virus or whole-cell)** — killed pathogen.
- Examples: inactivated polio (Salk IPV), hepatitis A, rabies (HDCV), influenza (inactivated), some COVID-19 vaccines (CoronaVac, Covaxin).
- Pros: safe; can be used in immunocompromised.
- Cons: weaker + shorter immunity; multiple doses + boosters; often weak CD8.

**Protein subunit** — purified or recombinant proteins.
- Examples: hepatitis B (yeast-produced HBsAg), acellular pertussis, HPV (VLPs of L1 capsid), shingles (Shingrix — recombinant VZV gE + AS01 adjuvant), RSV (preF antigen; arexvy, abrysvo).
- Pros: very safe; defined composition; scalable.
- Cons: need adjuvant; often weaker than live; weaker CD8.

**Conjugate vaccines** — polysaccharide antigen chemically linked to carrier protein → converts T-independent → T-dependent response, generating memory + functional in infants.
- Examples: **PCV13/PCV20** (pneumococcal), **Hib** (*Haemophilus influenzae* type b), **MenACWY** + **MenB** (meningococcal).
- Transformed pediatric infectious disease — Hib + pneumococcal disease in children plummeted (Hib disease >99% reduction).

**mRNA vaccines** — modified mRNA encoding antigen, encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs).
- **Katalin Karikó + Drew Weissman** (Nobel 2023): demonstrated that **modified nucleosides** (pseudouridine, 1-methylpseudouridine) reduce TLR7/8 + RIG-I sensing of mRNA → less innate immunogenicity, more translation. Foundational.
- **LNPs** (Cullis, MacLachlan + others): ionizable lipids + cholesterol + PEG-lipid + helper lipid; protect mRNA + mediate endosomal escape + cytosolic delivery. Critical co-invention.
- **COVID-19** mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2, Moderna mRNA-1273) — first mRNA vaccines approved (Dec 2020); deployed at unprecedented scale; saved millions of lives.
- Now extending to: influenza (Moderna, Pfizer trials), RSV (Moderna mRESVIA 2024), CMV, HIV, malaria, personalized cancer vaccines (BioNTech BNT122 + Moderna mRNA-4157 + Genentech RO7198457; melanoma + pancreatic + KEYNOTE-942).

**Viral-vector vaccines** — replication-defective virus delivering antigen-encoding DNA/RNA.
- Examples: adenovirus (ChAdOx1/AZ COVID-19 vaccine, Janssen Ad26 COVID-19, Sputnik V, Ebola rVSV-ZEBOV — Merck), measles vectors, smallpox vector.
- Pros: strong CD8 + Ab; single-dose can be effective.
- Cons: anti-vector immunity (limits boosting), rare thrombosis (adenoviral COVID).

**Adjuvants** — enhance + shape the response by engaging innate immunity:
- **Alum** (aluminum salts): >90 yrs of use; Th2-skewing; weak innate stimulator (NLRP3 + DAMPs).
- **MF59 + AS03** (oil-in-water squalene emulsions): used in influenza vaccines + pandemic preparedness.
- **AS01** (MPL + QS-21 in liposome): TLR4 (MPL) + saponin (QS-21) agonist combo; used in **Shingrix** + **malaria RTS,S** + **R21** vaccines.
- **CpG (TLR9)** — Heplisav-B (hepatitis B); strong Th1.
- **MPL alone, ISA, GLA-SE, polyIC** — various combinations under development.

**Live-attenuated + viral-vector + mRNA** drive **broad** responses (CD4 + CD8 + antibody); **subunit + inactivated** drive primarily antibody. Choice depends on pathogen biology + risk-benefit + manufacturing constraints.

slides.title: Landmark vaccination programs: smallpox to COVID-19
slides.body:
**Smallpox eradication (1980)** — the first + only human disease eradicated by vaccination.
- Variola virus killed ~300M people in the 20th century alone; case-fatality ~30%.
- Jenner 1796 → vaccinia-based vaccines globally → **WHO Intensified Eradication Programme (1967-1977; D.A. Henderson)**: ring vaccination strategy (vaccinate contacts of cases — exploits ~1 wk smallpox incubation longer than vaccine immunity onset), aggressive surveillance, bifurcated-needle delivery, freeze-dried vaccine.
- Last natural case: Somalia 1977. **WHO declared eradication May 1980**. One of the greatest achievements in public health.

**Polio** — global eradication ongoing.
- Salk **inactivated** vaccine (1955) + Sabin **oral live-attenuated** vaccine (1961) → near-eradication.
- Global Polio Eradication Initiative (1988): >99.9% reduction. Endemic only in Afghanistan + Pakistan (wild-type 1) as of 2024. Vaccine-derived poliovirus circulation has complicated final eradication; novel **nOPV2** being deployed.

**HPV — Ian Frazer + Jian Zhou + Harald zur Hausen**:
- **zur Hausen (Nobel 2008)**: established HPV as the cause of cervical cancer (1980s+) — one of the most consequential medical discoveries of the 20th century. ~5% of human cancers are HPV-related (cervical, anal, oropharyngeal, vulvar, vaginal, penile).
- **Frazer + Zhou** (University of Queensland 1991): showed HPV L1 capsid protein self-assembles into virus-like particles (VLPs) — basis of all HPV vaccines.
- **Gardasil (Merck)** + **Cervarix (GSK)** + **Gardasil-9** — VLP subunit vaccines; >90% efficacy against high-risk HPV-associated cancer when given before exposure. Now standard at age 9-12 + catch-up. Multi-country data show falling cervical cancer incidence; first cancer being eliminated by vaccination.

**RSV vaccines (2023-2024)** — historically failed (1960s formalin-inactivated vaccine caused enhanced disease + child deaths — Th2 + immune-complex pathology).
- Solved by **McLellan + Graham** (NIH/Vanderbilt): solved structure of pre-fusion F protein → **DS-Cav1** stabilized prefusion antigen.
- Approved: **GSK Arexvy** + **Pfizer Abrysvo** for older adults + maternal immunization (passive transfer to neonate); **Moderna mRESVIA** mRNA vaccine (2024). Same prefusion-stabilization principle applies to coronavirus spike + paramyxoviruses.
- **Nirsevimab** (long-acting monoclonal antibody, FcRn-engineered) — passive immunization of infants; transformative for the 2023-24 RSV season.

**COVID-19 vaccines (2020-2021)** — the fastest vaccines ever developed.
- Sequence published Jan 11 2020; **Pfizer-BioNTech** + **Moderna** mRNA vaccines authorized Dec 2020 — under 12 months from sequence to deployment.
- Built on decades of prior work: **Karikó-Weissman modified nucleosides**, LNP delivery, **McLellan-Graham prefusion-spike** (2017 work on MERS + RSV), Operation Warp Speed, Phase III trials in parallel with manufacturing scale-up.
- Saved an estimated 14-20 million lives in the first year. Most efficient + widely-administered vaccines ever.
- Adenovirus-vector (J&J Ad26, AstraZeneca ChAdOx1) + protein subunit (Novavax — Matrix-M adjuvant) + inactivated (CoronaVac) — global access matters.
- Established **mRNA platform** as production-ready for many subsequent indications: flu, RSV, CMV, HIV, malaria, cancer.

**Universal influenza** — frontier:
- HA stem (conserved) targeting → Krammer + Nachbagauer; multiple trials.
- mRNA-based multi-strain (Moderna mRNA-1010, Pfizer flu mRNA, Sanofi).
- Computationally-optimized broadly reactive antigens (COBRA — Ross).

**HIV vaccine** — most studied + most challenging:
- RV144 (Thai trial 2009) → 31% efficacy; only positive HIV vaccine trial.
- Germline-targeting + sequential boosting → IAVI G001 (2022) — first-in-human data showing on-target germline-engagement.
- BG505 mosaic (Nussenzweig + Schief) — stabilized SOSIP env trimers.
- bNAb passive immunization (3BNC117, 10-1074, VRC01) — long-acting prophylaxis as alternative or bridge.

Vaccinology has moved from empirical (Jenner 1796) to **rational, structure-based + immunology-driven** design — yet Jenner's principle remains: deliberate exposure to non-pathogenic antigen → protective immunity.

question.question: Derive why pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) work in infants while polysaccharide-only (PPSV23) does not
question.goal: Reason from B-cell biology + T-cell help why a conjugate vaccine succeeds in infants where a pure polysaccharide vaccine fails.

steps.prompt: Polysaccharides are T-independent type 2 antigens. What kind of B-cell response do they elicit?

acceptedAnswers: Polysaccharides cross-link many BCRs → IgM-dominated, short-lived, no class-switching, no memory, no germinal centers

hints: What can B cells do without Tfh help?
steps.reveal: T-independent type 2 antigens (capsular polysaccharides) cross-link many BCRs on marginal-zone + B-1 cells → IgM (some IgG2) plasmablasts → short-lived, no germinal centers, no robust class switching (especially in infants whose marginal-zone B cells mature slowly + whose Tfh help is limited). Memory is poor; revaccination does not boost.

steps.prompt: Why are infants particularly poor responders to polysaccharide-only vaccines (e.g., PPSV23)?

acceptedAnswers: Infants <2 yr have immature marginal-zone B cells + limited T-independent B-cell responses + cannot generate strong IgG memory to polysaccharides

hints: Splenic + marginal-zone development is gradual through age ~2.
steps.reveal: Marginal-zone B cells + B-1 cells (which mediate T-independent responses) mature gradually through age 2-5; consequently, T-independent polysaccharide vaccines (PPSV23) have poor efficacy under age 2 + variable in older children. Infants are precisely the population at highest risk of invasive pneumococcal + Hib disease.

steps.prompt: How does covalent conjugation of polysaccharide to a carrier protein (CRM197, tetanus toxoid, etc.) change the response?

acceptedAnswers: B cell binds polysaccharide, internalizes whole conjugate, presents carrier-peptide on MHC-II to Tfh that helps the polysaccharide-specific B cell — converting to T-dependent response with germinal centers + memory + class-switched IgG

hints: BCR sees polysaccharide; MHC-II + Tfh see carrier protein.
steps.reveal: **The conjugate trick**: B cell binds polysaccharide via its BCR → internalizes the whole conjugate → degrades the carrier protein in endosomes → presents carrier-derived peptides on MHC-II. A Tfh cell specific for the carrier protein (primed by DCs + GCs) provides CD40L + IL-21 → polysaccharide-specific B cell undergoes germinal-center reaction → class switching to IgG, SHM, affinity maturation, long-lived plasma cells + memory B cells. Now the polysaccharide-specific clone benefits from full T-dependent immunity even though its BCR sees only sugar.

steps.prompt: Why has this transformed pediatric infectious disease?

acceptedAnswers: Hib invasive disease nearly eliminated; pneumococcal invasive disease massively reduced (>90% in vaccine serotypes); meningococcal protection in infants — saved millions of lives globally

hints: Hib + PCV impact on pediatric morbidity + mortality.
steps.reveal: Hib conjugate (1990s): >99% reduction in invasive Hib disease in vaccinated populations. PCV7/PCV13/PCV15/PCV20 + MenACWY conjugates: massive reduction in pneumococcal + meningococcal disease in infants + indirect herd protection across age groups. Estimated millions of lives saved. The polysaccharide-to-conjugate transition is one of the most consequential applied-immunology innovations of the 20th century — directly built on Tfh + germinal-center + class-switch biology.

question.question: Why was the Karikó-Weissman Nobel 2023 awarded for modified-nucleoside mRNA — what problem did pseudouridine + 1-methylpseudouridine solve?
options: **Katalin Karikó + Drew Weissman** (Nobel 2023) discovered that incorporating **modified nucleosides** (pseudouridine, later 1-methylpseudouridine + 5-methylcytidine) into in-vitro-transcribed mRNA dramatically reduces sensing by innate-immune RNA sensors — TLR7/8 (endosomal ssRNA), RIG-I/MDA5 (cytosolic dsRNA), PKR. This solved two coupled problems: (1) **innate-immune over-activation** (unmodified mRNA triggered massive IFN + cytokine response → systemic toxicity + translational shutdown), + (2) **poor protein expression** (PKR phosphorylates eIF2α, blocking translation; modified mRNA evades this). Result: dramatically higher antigen expression + minimal systemic inflammation. Combined with **LNP delivery** (Cullis, MacLachlan, Anderson, Madden et al.), modified-mRNA became practical → enabled the Pfizer-BioNTech BNT162b2 + Moderna mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccines (deployed Dec 2020 — under 12 months from genome sequence to deployment). Saved 14-20 million lives in year 1. Now extends to flu, RSV (mRESVIA), CMV, HIV, malaria, personalized cancer vaccines (BNT122, mRNA-4157 — practice-changing melanoma + pancreatic data). One of the highest-impact biomedical advances of the century.
question.explanation: Karikó + Weissman (Nobel 2023) showed pseudouridine + 1-methylpseudouridine in mRNA reduces TLR7/8 + RIG-I/MDA5 + PKR sensing — solving over-activation + translation shutdown. Combined with LNP delivery, enabled the Pfizer-BioNTech + Moderna COVID-19 mRNA vaccines + the broader mRNA platform (flu, RSV, CMV, HIV, malaria, cancer).

hints: Why is unmodified IVT mRNA so inflammatory?
slides.workedSolution: Karikó + Weissman discovered modified nucleosides (pseudouridine, 1-methylpseudouridine) dramatically reduce mRNA recognition by innate sensors (TLR7/8, RIG-I/MDA5, PKR), enabling robust antigen expression with minimal inflammation. Combined with LNP delivery → mRNA vaccines (COVID-19 BNT162b2 + mRNA-1273, RSV, flu, cancer).

question.question: Designing a universal influenza vaccine
question.prompt: You are the lead immunologist on a universal influenza vaccine program. (a) Why has 70 yrs of effort + thousands of recurrent flu vaccines failed to provide durable, strain-transcending protection — what role does **antigenic drift + shift** in HA + NA play? (b) What is the conceptual argument for targeting the **HA stem** (Krammer, Nachbagauer) vs the variable HA head? (c) How would you combine **mRNA delivery** (Karikó-Weissman platform) + **immunogen design** (sequential boost, stem-only, mosaic HA) + **adjuvants** (MF59, AS01) to drive bnAb responses against HA stem? (d) What endpoints (microneutralization, ADCC, MAARI) + clinical-trial designs would actually demonstrate breadth + durability?

question.question: Write the standard formula for vaccine efficacy (VE) given the attack rates in vaccinated (ARV) + unvaccinated (ARU) groups.
question.hint: Relative risk reduction in vaccinated vs unvaccinated.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how vaccinology progressed from Jenner's empirical 1796 cowpox to the structure-based, mRNA-enabled, rational design of the 21st century.
question.rubric: Mentions: **Jenner (1796)** — empirical cowpox-smallpox cross-protection. **Pasteur (1880s)** — deliberate attenuation. **Behring-Kitasato (1890)** — serotherapy + antibodies. **Salk + Sabin (1950s-60s)** — inactivated + live polio vaccines. **Smallpox eradication (1980)** — first eradicated disease, ring vaccination + WHO programme. **Hib + pneumococcal conjugates (1990s+)** — eliminated leading pediatric infections. **HPV VLP vaccines** (Frazer + Zhou; zur Hausen Nobel 2008) — first cancer vaccines. **Structure-based design** (McLellan-Graham prefusion F → RSV; same principle to SARS-CoV-2 spike). **mRNA platform** (Karikó-Weissman Nobel 2023 + LNPs) → COVID-19 vaccines deployed in under 12 months → mRNA flu, RSV, CMV, HIV, malaria, cancer (BNT122, mRNA-4157). **Adjuvants** (alum, MF59, AS01, CpG) shape responses. Vaccinology is now a rational discipline integrating structural biology, immunology, manufacturing science, + AI — yet Jenner's principle of deliberate priming remains the foundation.
